content.title: Jobless Claims Fall. What That Means for Fed Rate Cuts.
content.summary: The number of Americans filing for initial unemployment benefits dropped last week, suggesting the labor market is still in a relatively good place as the year draws to a close.  The jobless claims number fell by 10,000 to 214,00 for the week ended Dec. 20, according to Labor Department data published on Wednesday.  The drop in jobless claims is good news for the economy, although a stronger labor market may weaken the case for the Federal Reserve to carry on cutting interest rates in early 2026, which would be disappointing for the market.

content.title: Gold and Silver Are Finishing a Record-Setting Year With…More Records
content.summary: 1722 ET – Gold and silver rose to new records on Friday, which is what they’ve been doing for much of 2025.  The most-active gold futures contract on Friday closed at a record for the 51st time this year, according to Dow Jones Market Data.  The precious metal’s price has surged 66% this year to $4,387.30 a troy ounce.
